title: The Hidden Economic Power of Healthy Soils
gist: Up to 40% of the world's land is degraded, threatening businesses and economies that depend on it, yet soil health remains almost entirely absent from how governments, companies and investors price value and risk.

insights.claim: Up to 40% of the world's land is degraded, affecting more than 3.2 billion people and increasingly putting at risk the businesses and economies that depend on healthy land.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A resource risk of this scale (3.2bn people, 40% of land) sits largely outside conventional business and investment risk models, implying mispriced exposure across land-dependent sectors like agriculture, food, and commodities.
insights.quote: Up to 40% of the world’s land is degraded, affecting more than 3.2 billion people and increasingly putting the businesses and economies that depend on healthy land at risk.
insights.locator: Up to 40% of the world's land is degraded

insights.claim: Land degradation is driven by unsustainable land use and economic incentives that prioritize short-term production over long-term soil health, and these pressures are compounded by climate change.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Points to a structural, incentive-driven root cause (short-termism in production decisions) rather than just a climate problem, meaning fixes require realigning economic incentives, not only environmental policy.
insights.quote: These pressures are driven by unsustainable land use and economic incentives that prioritize short-term production over long-term soil health, compounded by climate change.
insights.locator: These pressures are driven by unsustainable land use

themes.theme: Soil as an Unpriced Strategic Asset

insights.claim: Healthy soil functions as a strategic economic asset, not merely an environmental or agricultural concern, yet it remains largely invisible in how governments, businesses and investors assess value and manage risk.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Identifies a blind spot in valuation and risk frameworks across public and private sectors; investors who start pricing soil health early could gain an edge in assessing land-dependent asset risk before it becomes mainstream.
insights.quote: Yet soil remains largely invisible in how governments, businesses and investors assess value and manage risk.
insights.locator: Healthy soil is not only an environmental or agricultural imperative

themes.theme: The Business Case for Soil Investment

insights.claim: Soil dependency is business dependency: healthy soils support productivity, resilience and long-term value, while degraded soils create growing risks, and investing in soil health is framed as both urgent and achievable.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Reframes soil health as a direct lever on corporate resilience and valuation rather than a peripheral sustainability line item, suggesting a potential future channel for ESG/risk disclosure or capital allocation.
insights.quote: soil dependency is business dependency. Healthy soils support productivity, resilience and long-term value, while degraded soils create growing risks.
insights.locator: This paper makes the business case for action
